You are auditing Android/Kotlin AI-agent "skill" files for the "Testing & debugging" topic across up to three source repos that are being merged into ONE Claude Code plugin. When multiple skills auto-trigger on the same code, contradictory guidance is a real defect.

Read the FULL content of every SKILL.md in these directories, plus any references/*.md files inside them (use Glob or Bash 'ls -R' first to discover reference files):

- [ahmed] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/everything-claude-code-mobile/skills/mobile-testing/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)

- [chris] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/skills/skills/compose-ui-testing-patterns/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [rcosteira] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/android-skills/plugins/android-skills/skills/android-testing/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)
- [rcosteira] /Users/oleksandr.priadko/Documents/StudioProjects/sub/android-skills/plugins/android-skills/skills/android-debugging/  (read SKILL.md AND any references/*.md inside)

Produce:
1. contradictions — cases where two sources give ACTUALLY OPPOSING advice on the SAME specific technical point (not merely different depth or wording of the same principle). Name both sources (labels: "ahmed" / "chris" / "rcosteira"), state each claim, and cite evidence (file path + the specific lines/quote).
2. bugs — code that is broken, will not compile, or is technically WRONG (e.g. catches and swallows CancellationException, loses state across config change, references undefined symbols, wrong plugin/order). severity: critical | major | minor. Cite the file + evidence.
3. depthComparison — which source is most detailed/actionable here and why.
4. uniqueValue — what each source covers that the OTHERS DO NOT (worth keeping regardless of who dominates).

Be precise; cite real file content. Do NOT invent contradictions where sources only differ in depth — that is the most common false positive. Set cluster="testing".

6	# iOS Testing
7	
8	Testing patterns for Swift and SwiftUI apps.
9	
10	## Unit Tests
11	
12	### Basic Unit Test
13	
14	```swift
15	import XCTest
16	@testable import MyApp
17	
18	class UserViewModelTests: XCTestCase {
19	    var sut: UserViewModel!
20	    var mockService: MockUserService!
21	
22	    override func setUp() {
23	        super.setUp()
24	        mockService = MockUserService()
25	        sut = UserViewModel(service: mockService)
26	    }
27	
28	    override func tearDown() {
29	        sut = nil
30	        mockService = nil
31	        super.tearDown()
32	    }
33	
34	    func testLoadUsers_whenSuccessful_populatesUsers() async throws {
35	        // Given
36	        let expectedUsers = [User.mock1, User.mock2]
37	        mockService.usersToReturn = expectedUsers
38	
39	        // When
40	        await sut.loadUsers()
41	
42	        // Then
43	        XCTAssertEqual(sut.users, expectedUsers)
44	        XCTAssertFalse(sut.isLoading)
45	        XCTAssertNil(sut.errorMessage)
46	    }
47	
48	    func testLoadUsers_whenFailure_setsErrorMessage() async throws {
49	        // Given
50	        mockService.shouldThrowError = true
51	
52	        // When
53	        await sut.loadUsers()
54	
55	        // Then
56	        XCTAssertTrue(sut.users.isEmpty)
57	        XCTAssertNotNil(sut.errorMessage)
58	    }
59	}
60	```
61	
62	### Mocking
63	
64	```swift
65	// ✅ Protocol-based mocking
66	protocol UserServiceProtocol {
67	    func getUsers() async throws -> [User]
68	}
69	
70	class MockUserService: UserServiceProtocol {
71	    var usersToReturn: [User] = []
72	    var shouldThrowError = false
73	    var getUsersCalled = false
74	
75	    func getUsers() async throws -> [User] {
76	        getUsersCalled = true
77	        if shouldThrowError {
78	            throw NetworkError.noConnection
79	        }
80	        return usersToReturn
81	    }
82	}
83	
84	// ✅ Verify method calls
85	func testRefreshButton_callsService() async {
86	    // When
87	    await sut.refresh()
88	
89	    // Then
90	    XCTAssertTrue(mockService.getUsersCalled)
91	}
92	```
93	
94	## Async Testing
95	
96	```swift
97	func testAsyncOperation_completesSuccessfully() async throws {
98	    // Given
99	    let expectation = expectation(description: "Async completes")
100	
101	    // When
102	    Task {
103	        await sut.asyncOperation()
104	        expectation.fulfill()
105	    }
106	
107	    // Then
108	    await fulfillment(of: [expectation], timeout: 1.0)
109	}
110	
111	// ✅ Swift async/await
112	func testAsyncFetch_returnsUsers() async throws {
113	    let users = try await sut.fetchUsers()
114	    XCTAssertFalse(users.isEmpty)
115	}
116	```
117	
118	## Property Testing
119	
120	```swift
121	func testUserValidation_validEmails() {
122	    let validEmails = [
123	        "test@example.com",
124	        "user.name@example.co.uk",
125	        "user+tag@example.com"
126	    ]
127	
128	    for email in validEmails {
129	        XCTAssertTrue(Validator.isValidEmail(email), "Failed for: \(email)")
130	    }
131	}
132	
133	func testUserValidation_invalidEmails() {
134	    let invalidEmails = [
135	        "invalid",
136	        "@example.com",
137	        "user@",
138	        "user @example.com"
139	    ]
140	
141	    for email in invalidEmails {
142	        XCTAssertFalse(Validator.isValidEmail(email), "Passed for: \(email)")
143	    }
144	}
145	```
146	
147	## UI Tests
148	
149	### Basic UI Test
150	
151	```swift
152	import XCTest
153	
154	class LoginUITests: XCTestCase {
155	    var app: XCUIApplication!
156	
157	    override func setUp() {
158	        super.setUp()
159	        continueAfterFailure = false
160	        app = XCUIApplication()
161	        app.launchArguments = ["--uitesting"]
162	        app.launch()
163	    }
164	
165	    func testLoginButton_enabledWhenFieldsFilled() {
166	        // When
167	        let emailField = app.textFields["emailField"]
168	        let passwordField = app.secureTextFields["passwordField"]
169	        let loginButton = app.buttons["loginButton"]
170	
171	        // Then
172	        XCTAssertFalse(loginButton.isEnabled)
173	
174	        // When
175	        emailField.tap()
176	        emailField.typeText("test@example.com")
177	
178	        passwordField.tap()
179	        passwordField.typeText("password123")
180	
181	        // Then
182	        XCTAssertTrue(loginButton.isEnabled)
183	    }
184	
185	    func testSuccessfulLogin_navigatesToHome() {
186	        // Given
187	        app.textFields["emailField"].tap()
188	        app.textFields["emailField"].typeText("test@example.com")
189	
190	        app.secureTextFields["passwordField"].tap()
191	        app.secureTextFields["passwordField"].typeText("password123")
192	
193	        // When
194	        app.buttons["loginButton"].tap()
195	
196	        // Then
197	        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["welcomeMessage"].exists)
198	    }
199	}
200	```
201	
202	### Snapshot Testing
203	
204	```swift
205	// ✅ Using View snapshot testing
206	import SwiftUI
207	import XCTest
208	
209	struct UserCard_Previews: PreviewProvider {
210	    static var previews: some View {
211	        UserCard(user: .mock)
212	    }
213	}
214	
215	// Snapshot test
216	func testUserCard_snapshot() {
217	    let view = UserCard(user: .mock)
218	    assertSnapshot(matching: view, as: .image(layout: .sizeThatFits))
219	}

222	## Testing SwiftUI Views
223	
224	```swift
225	import XCTest
226	import ViewInspector  // https://github.com/nalexn/ViewInspector
227	
228	class UserRowTests: XCTestCase {
229	    func testUserRow_displaysUserName() throws {
230	        let user = User(id: "1", name: "John Doe", email: "john@example.com")
231	        let view = UserRow(user: user)
232	
233	        let text = try view.inspect().find(ViewType.Text.self).string()
234	        XCTAssertEqual(text, "John Doe")
235	    }
236	
237	    func testUserRow_tapping_callsAction() throws {
238	        let user = User(id: "1", name: "John", email: "john@example.com")
239	        var tapped = false
240	        let view = UserRow(user: user, onTap: { tapped = true })
241	
242	        try view.inspect().find(ViewType.Button.self).tap()
243	
244	        XCTAssertTrue(tapped)
245	    }
246	}
247	```
248	
249	## Test Helpers
250	
251	```swift
252	// ✅ Test doubles
253	extension User {
254	    static let mock1 = User(id: "1", name: "John", email: "john@example.com")
255	    static let mock2 = User(id: "2", name: "Jane", email: "jane@example.com")
256	}
257	
258	// ✅ Wait helpers
259	func waitForElementToExist(
260	    _ element: XCUIElement,
261	    timeout: TimeInterval = 5.0
262	) -> Bool {
263	    let existsPredicate = NSPredicate(format: "exists == true")
264	    let expectation = expectation(for: existsPredicate, evaluatedWith: element)
265	
266	    let result = XCTWaiter.wait(for: [expectation], timeout: timeout)
267	    return result == .completed
268	}
269	```
270	
271	## Performance Tests
272	
273	```swift
274	func testUserParsing_performance() {
275	    let jsonData = largeUserJSONData
276	
277	    measure {
278	        _ = try? JSONDecoder().decode([User].self, from: jsonData)
279	    }
280	}
281	```

283	## Test Organization
284	
285	```
286	Tests/
287	├── Unit/
288	│   ├── ViewModels/
289	│   │   ├── HomeViewModelTests.swift

305	
306	**Remember**: Tests are your safety net. Write them first (TDD) or alongside your code, but always maintain them.

5	
6	# Mobile Verification Skill
7	
8	Comprehensive testing workflow with pass@k metrics for Android development reliability.
9	
10	## Philosophy
11	
12	**Single test runs lie.**
13	
14	A test that passes once might fail tomorrow. Verification loops run tests multiple times to reveal:
15	- Flaky tests (timing issues, async problems)
16	- Intermittent failures (resource contention)
17	- Reliability trends (improving vs degrading)
18	
19	## Pass@k Explained
20	
21	Pass@k = proportion of test iterations that passed
22	
23	```
24	Pass@3(test) = tests_passed / 3
25	
26	testLogin(): ✓✓✓ → Pass@3 = 3/3 = 1.0 (100%)
27	testLogout(): ✓✓✗ → Pass@3 = 2/3 = 0.67 (67%)
28	testRefresh(): ✗✗✗ → Pass@3 = 0/3 = 0.0 (0%)
29	```
30	
31	## Verification Levels
32	
33	### Quick Verification (k=2)
34	```
35	Purpose: Fast feedback during development
36	Usage: /mobile-verify --k=2
37	Time: ~2 minutes
38	When: After small changes, before commit
39	```
40	
41	### Standard Verification (k=3)
42	```
43	Purpose: Standard confidence level
44	Usage: /mobile-verify --k=3
45	Time: ~5 minutes
46	When: Before push, after feature complete
47	```
48	
49	### Thorough Verification (k=5)
50	```
51	Purpose: High confidence, flaky detection
52	Usage: /mobile-verify --k=5
53	Time: ~10 minutes
54	When: Before release, after refactor
55	```
56	
57	### Release Verification (k=10)
58	```
59	Purpose: Maximum confidence
60	Usage: /mobile-verify --k=10
61	Time: ~20 minutes
62	When: Production release, critical bugs
63	```
64	
65	## Test Type Strategies
66	
67	### Unit Tests (JUnit)
68	
69	**Characteristics:**
70	- Fast: ~1-2 seconds per test
71	- Isolated: No Android dependencies
72	- Reliable: Should be Pass@k = 1.0
73	
74	**Target Pass@k:** ≥ 0.95 (95%)
75	
76	**Common Flaky Causes:**
77	- Async operations without proper waiting
78	- Date/time dependencies
79	- Random data generation
80	- Static state leakage
81	
82	**Fix Strategies:**
83	```kotlin
84	// Bad: Flaky
85	@Test
86	fun testLoadData() {
87	    viewModel.loadData()
88	    assert(viewModel.state.value is Loaded)
89	}
90	
91	// Good: Stable
92	@Test
93	fun testLoadData() = runTest {
94	    viewModel.loadData()
95	    advanceUntilIdle()
96	    assert(viewModel.state.value is Loaded)
97	}
98	```
99	
100	### UI Tests (Espresso)
101	
102	**Characteristics:**
103	- Slow: ~5-10 seconds per test
104	- Device-dependent: Need emulator/device
105	- Fragile: UI changes break tests
106	
107	**Target Pass@k:** ≥ 0.80 (80%)
108	
109	**Common Flaky Causes:**
110	- Idling resource not registered
111	- Animation interference
112	- Screen rotation
113	- Network timeouts
114	
115	**Fix Strategies:**
116	```kotlin
117	// Register idling resources
118	@IdlingResource
119	val countingIdlingResource = CountingIdlingResource("api")
120	
121	// Disable animations
122	@get:Rule
123	val disableAnimationsRule = DisableAnimationsRule()
124	```
125	
126	### Compose Tests
127	
128	**Characteristics:**
129	- Fast: ~1-3 seconds per test
130	- UI-level: Tests Composable behavior
131	- Modern: Uses Compose Testing framework
132	
133	**Target Pass@k:** ≥ 0.90 (90%)
134	
135	**Common Flaky Causes:**
136	- Recomposition timing
137	- State hoisting issues
138	- Animation interference
139	
140	**Fix Strategies:**
141	```kotlin
142	@Composable
143	fun TestComposable(content: @Composable () -> Unit) {
144	    CompositionLocalProvider(
145	        LocalInspectionMode provides true
146	    ) {
147	        content()
148	    }
149	}
150	```
151	
152	## Verification Workflow
153	
154	### During Development
155	
156	```bash
157	# 1. Write test
158	# 2. Quick verify
159	/mobile-verify --class=NewTest --k=2
160	
161	# 3. Fix if fails
162	# 4. Standard verify
163	/mobile-verify --class=NewTest --k=3
164	```
165	
166	### Before Commit
167	
168	```bash
169	# Verify changed modules only
170	/mobile-verify --module=$(git diff --name-only | head -1) --k=2
171	```
172	
173	### Before Push
174	
175	```bash
176	# Full verification
177	/mobile-verify --k=3
178	```
179	
180	### Before Release
181	
182	```bash
183	# Thorough verification with flaky detection
184	/mobile-verify --k=5 --flaky
185	```
186	
187	## Interpreting Results
188	
189	### Pass@k Scores
190	
191	| Score | Meaning | Action |
192	|-------|---------|--------|
193	| 1.0 | Perfect | Celebrate |
194	| 0.8-0.9 | Excellent | Monitor |
195	| 0.6-0.7 | Good | Investigate |
196	| 0.4-0.5 | Fair | Fix needed |
197	| 0.0-0.3 | Poor | Block release |
198	
199	### Trends
200	
201	Track pass@k over time:
202	
203	```
204	Week 1: Pass@3 = 0.85
205	Week 2: Pass@3 = 0.87  ↗ Improving
206	Week 3: Pass@3 = 0.82  ↘ Degraded - investigate!
207	Week 4: Pass@3 = 0.88  ↗ Recovered
208	```
209	
210	### Flaky Test Patterns
211	
212	| Pattern | Likely Cause |
213	|---------|--------------|
214	| Fails on iteration 1 only | Cold start issue |
215	| Fails randomly | Async timing |
216	| Fails on specific iteration | Resource leak |
217	| Fails in parallel only | Shared state |
218	
219	## Fixing Flaky Tests
220	
221	### Step 1: Identify Pattern
222	
223	```bash
224	/mobile-verify --flaky --k=10
225	```
226	
227	Look for patterns in failures.
228	
229	### Step 2: Add Diagnostics
230	
231	```kotlin
232	@Test
233	fun flakyTest() = runTest {
234	    val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
235	    // ... test code ...
236	    val duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime
237	    Log.d("Test", "Duration: $duration ms")  // Check for timing issues
238	}
239	```
240	
241	### Step 3: Apply Fix
242	
243	Common fixes:
244	- Add `advanceUntilIdle()` for coroutines
245	- Add `IdlingResource` for network
246	- Disable animations for UI tests
247	- Use `@UiThreadTest` for main thread work
248	- Add explicit waits for async operations
249	
250	### Step 4: Verify Fix
251	
252	```bash
253	/mobile-verify --class=FixedTest --k=5
254	```
255	
256	Target: Pass@5 = 1.0
257	
258	## Integration
259	
260	### With Checkpoints
261	
262	Create checkpoint before verification:
263	```bash
264	/mobile-checkpoint save pre-verify
265	/mobile-verify --k=3
266	```
267	
268	### With Memory
269	
270	Track pass@k in memory:
271	```json
272	{
273	    "test-coverage": {
274	        "passAt3": 0.87,
275	        "trend": "improving",
276	        "flakyTests": []
277	    }
278	}
279	```
280	
281	### With Instincts
282	
283	Learn testing patterns:
284	```json
285	{
286	    "id": "test-coroutine-async",
287	    "description": "Always use runTest + advanceUntilIdle for ViewModel tests",
288	    "confidence": 0.95
289	}
290	```
291	
292	## Thresholds by Context
293	
294	| Context | Pass@k Threshold | Rationale |
295	|---------|------------------|-----------|
296	| Unit tests | 0.95 | Should be deterministic |
297	| UI tests | 0.80 | More fragile, device-dependent |
298	| Compose tests | 0.90 | Better than Espresso, more stable |
299	| Integration tests | 0.70 | Complex, more variables |
300	| E2E tests | 0.60 | Full system, many variables |
301	
302	## Best Practices
303	
304	1. **Start High, Go Low**: Use k=5 for investigation, k=3 for routine
305	2. **Fix Flaky Fast**: Don't tolerate flaky tests
306	3. **Track Trends**: Monitor pass@k over time
307	4. **Context Matters**: UI tests can have lower thresholds than unit
308	5. **Block Release**: Failed verification should block releases
309	
310	---
311	
312	**Remember**: A test that sometimes passes is worse than no test at all. It gives false confidence.
313

2	name: compose-ui-testing-patterns
3	description: Use when writing or reviewing Jetpack Compose UI tests, screenshot tests, previews, semantics assertions, fake image loading, keyboard input, focus assertions, interaction state (hover/pressed/focused), or tests for plain state-driven UI composables.
4	---
5	
6	# Compose: UI testing patterns
7	
8	## Core principle
9	
10	Test the smallest UI contract that proves the behavior. Prefer plain state-driven UI tests with callbacks. Add integration only when lifecycle, navigation, DI, or platform behavior is the thing under test.
11	
12	## Test target choice
13	
14	| What you need to prove | Test shape |
15	|---|---|
16	| Text, button, loading/error branch, conditional content | Plain UI Compose test |
17	| Callback wiring from click/input | Plain UI Compose test |
18	| Focus navigation or keyboard behavior | Compose test with key input |
19	| Visual layout, clipping, elevation, typography, image composition | Screenshot test |
20	| State holder updates UI correctly | State holder/unit test plus one wiring smoke test |
21	| Hover, pressed, focused, dragged interaction state | Plain UI test with MutableInteractionSource |
22	| Navigation, lifecycle, DI integration | Integration test |
23	
24	## Prefer plain UI tests
25	
26	If the screen has a state holder/UI split, test the plain UI composable:
27	
28	```kotlin
29	composeTestRule.setContent {
30	    ProfileScreen(
31	        state = ProfileUiState(name = "Ada", canSave = true),
32	        onNameChange = {},
33	        onSaveClick = { saved = true },
34	        onBackClick = {},
35	    )
36	}
37	
38	composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Ada").assertIsDisplayed()
39	composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Save").performClick()
40	
41	assertThat(saved).isTrue()
42	```
43	
44	This avoids constructing ViewModels, components, repositories, navigation, and dependency graphs for layout behavior.
45	
46	## Semantics first
47	
48	Assert semantics when behavior is semantic:
49	
50	- Text exists: `onNodeWithText`.
51	- Button is enabled/disabled: `assertIsEnabled`, `assertIsNotEnabled`.
52	- Content is selected/focused/toggled: use semantics assertions.
53	- Content is absent: `assertDoesNotExist`.
54	
55	Use test tags for nodes that have no stable user-visible text or where multiple nodes share text. Do not use tags as the first choice for all assertions; user-visible semantics are usually stronger.
56	
57	## Callback testing
58	
59	Use simple counters or captured values:
60	
61	```kotlin
62	var selectedId: String? = null
63	
64	composeTestRule.setContent {
65	    ItemList(
66	        items = listOf(ItemUi("movie-1", "Movie")),
67	        onItemClick = { selectedId = it },
68	    )
69	}
70	
71	composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Movie").performClick()
72	
73	assertThat(selectedId).isEqualTo("movie-1")
74	```
75	
76	For plain captured callback values, a direct assertion after the action is usually enough. Use `runOnIdle` when the assertion needs Compose to finish applying snapshot state, recomposition, or queued UI work before reading the result.
77	
78	## Interaction state with MutableInteractionSource
79	
80	When a composable's appearance or behavior depends on interaction state (hover, focus, press, drag), inject a `MutableInteractionSource` and emit the desired state directly. Do not try to simulate pointer/mouse events to trigger interaction states — that approach is fragile, environment-dependent, and produces flaky tests.
81	
82	```kotlin
83	val interactionSource = MutableInteractionSource()
84	
85	composeTestRule.setContent {
86	    OutlinedButton(
87	        onClick = {},
88	        interactionSource = interactionSource,
89	    )
90	}
91	
92	// Assert default (un-hovered) state
93	composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("OutlinedButton").assertIsDisplayed()
94	
95	// Emit hover — interactionSource.emit is a suspend function,
96	// so call it from a test coroutine scope.
97	TestScope().launch {
98	    interactionSource.emit(HoverInteraction.Enter())
99	}
100	
101	composeTestRule.waitForIdle()
102	
103	// Assert the visual/semantic change that hover produces
104	// (e.g., border color, elevation, or capture for screenshot test)
105	composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("OutlinedButton").assertIsDisplayed()
106	```
107	
108	The same pattern works for `PressInteraction.Press` / `Release` / `Cancel`, `FocusInteraction.Focus` / `Unfocus`, and `DragInteraction.Start` / `Stop` / `Cancel`. Emit the entry interaction, `waitForIdle`, then assert the result.
109	
110	Key points:
111	
112	- **Always inject `MutableInteractionSource`** rather than relying on the default internal source. This gives you full control over state transitions.
113	- **Emit interactions from a coroutine scope** (e.g. `TestScope().launch { }`) since `emit` is a suspend function. Do not use `LaunchedEffect` — that is a production Compose effect, not a test tool.
114	- **Assert the *result* of the interaction** (visual change, semantic change, enabled state), not the interaction itself. The interaction source is a test *driver*, not the assertion target.
115	- **Use this for screenshot tests too** — emit the interaction state, then capture the screenshot for a deterministic hover/press/focus visual.
116	
117	## Keyboard and focus
118	
119	For keyboard, TV, and desktop UI, drive navigation with the same input model users use (keys/D-pad), not clicks alone. Assert focused semantics, not colors or scale; reserve screenshots for visual focus treatment.
120	
121	Details—focus graph, `FocusRequester`, restoration, key handlers, and test patterns: [`compose-focus-navigation`](../compose-focus-navigation/SKILL.md).
122	
123	## Screenshot tests
124	
125	Use screenshots for visual contracts that semantics cannot prove:
126	
127	- Layout spacing/alignment.
128	- Themed colors, typography, elevation, shadows.
129	- Image composition, gradients, overlays.
130	- Focus highlight appearance.
131	- Loading skeletons or dense visual states.
132	
133	Keep screenshot state deterministic:
134	
135	- Use fixed state data.
136	- Freeze clocks or animation progress when possible.
137	- Replace network/image loading with fake or preview handlers.
138	- Avoid asserting dynamic text such as current time unless controlled.
139	
140	## Fake images and platform services
141	
142	When image content is irrelevant, fake the loader and assert the requested model if that is the behavior. The exact hook depends on your image library; a project helper might look like this:
143	
144	```kotlin
145	val requestedModels = mutableListOf<Any?>()
146	
147	// Example helper, not a Compose API.
148	setContentWithFakeImageLoader { request ->
149	    requestedModels += request.data
150	    errorPainter()
151	}
152	```
153	
154	When image appearance matters, provide a deterministic local painter/bitmap instead of network data.
155	
156	## Common mistakes
157	
158	| Mistake | Fix |
159	|---|---|
160	| Constructing full app graph to test an error row | Test plain UI with `state = Error` |
161	| Testing click behavior through a ViewModel mock | Pass a callback and assert it was invoked |
162	| Screenshot test for simple text presence | Use semantics assertion |
163	| Semantics test for padding/color/focus ring | Use screenshot test |
164	| Test tags everywhere | Prefer text/content description/role when stable |
165	| UI test depends on real image loading/network/time | Fake or freeze the source |
166	| Simulating hover/press/focus with mouse or touch events | Inject `MutableInteractionSource` and emit the interaction |
167	| Relying on the default `InteractionSource` in tests | Pass `MutableInteractionSource` so you can control state |
168	| TV/keyboard UI tested with `performClick` only | Use key input and focus assertions; see [compose-focus-navigation](../compose-focus-navigation/SKILL.md) |
169	
170	## Red flags during review
171	
172	- "This UI test is flaky because images load slowly."
173	- A test uses production DI for simple rendering.
174	- A screenshot has random dates, clocks, remote images, or live data.
175	- Assertions only check that a node exists after performing an action, not that the callback/state change happened.
176	- Focus behavior is visually inspected but not asserted.
177	- A test uses `performMouseInput` or touch injection to trigger hover/press states instead of `MutableInteractionSource.emit`.
178	- A composable accepts `interactionSource` but tests don't inject `MutableInteractionSource`.
179

10	
11	# Android Testing
12	
13	Android-specific testing on a **test-first** foundation. This reference focuses on the test-first discipline plus the Compose-test traps that are easy to get wrong, not the basics of the three tiers, fakes over mocks, `runTest`, or Given-When-Then naming.
14	
15	## Test-first (the foundation)
16	
17	- **No production code without a failing test first.** Write the test, watch it fail (RED), write the minimal code to pass (GREEN), then refactor. A behaviour you never watched fail isn't proven.
18	- **A bug isn't fixed until a test that was red *because of the bug* is green.**
19	
20	This layers on top of any dedicated TDD discipline skill (`superpowers:test-driven-development`, `ace:test-driven-development`) but requires none. For *bootstrapping* the test stack from scratch (test DI, JUnit/Robolectric/Roborazzi/Paparazzi selection, the instrumented runner, Compose Preview Screenshot Testing, UI Automator, Jacoco), see Google's official [`testing-setup`](https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/testing/testing-setup) skill (`android skills add testing-setup`).
21	
22	## Compose tests now default to `StandardTestDispatcher`
23	
24	`createComposeRule()` / `runComposeUiTest {}` default to `StandardTestDispatcher` (matching `kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest`) — **there is no separate "v2" package.** It's gated by `androidx.compose.ui.test.ComposeUiTestFlags.isStandardTestDispatcherSupportEnabled` (defaults to `true`), so the regular `androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule` already uses it. To pin a scheduler, pass it through: `createComposeRule(effectContext = StandardTestDispatcher())`. Under this default, a `LaunchedEffect` that previously ran eagerly (the old `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` behaviour) may need an explicit `mainClock.advanceTimeBy(0)` / `runCurrent()` to drain queued work; set the flag `false` only to temporarily restore the legacy behaviour.
25	
26	**Two-schedulers trap** (the one coroutine-test gotcha worth stating): a `MainDispatcherRule`'s `TestDispatcher` and the dispatcher `runTest { }` creates have **separate** `TestCoroutineScheduler`s. Pass `mainRule.dispatcher` into `runTest(mainRule.dispatcher)` so `Dispatchers.Main` and the test body share one — otherwise `advanceUntilIdle()` flushes only one and assertions race the ViewModel.
27	
28	## Semantics first, `testTag` as fallback
29	
30	Prefer user-visible semantics over `testTag` — real users and screen readers see semantics; `testTag` is invisible to everyone except tests. Selector priority: (1) `onNodeWithText`; (2) `onNodeWithContentDescription`; (3) role/state matchers (`hasClickAction()`, `isSelected()`, `isFocused()`, `isEnabled()`); (4) `onNodeWithTag` **only** when there's no stable user-visible text or it's duplicated/ambiguous (lists of identical rows, per-locale copy, multiple instances). A text assertion survives refactors and exercises accessibility; a `testTag` assertion breaks the moment the tag changes and misses the user-facing regression.
31	
32	*(Counterview worth knowing: [skydoves/android-testing-skills](https://github.com/skydoves/android-testing-skills) argues tag-first for i18n robustness, backed by androidx/material3's own 1825 : 424 : 46 `testTag` : `onNodeWithText` : `onNodeWithContentDescription` ratio. Defensible if you have separate accessibility coverage; this skill defaults to semantics-first because it catches a class of bugs `testTag` never can.)*
33	
34	## Callbacks as test surfaces
35	
36	A composable's contract is "render state, emit callbacks" — test exactly that; don't route the assertion through a ViewModel mock.
37	
38	```kotlin
39	@Test fun `tapping article row invokes onArticleClick with id`() {
40	    var clickedId: String? = null
41	    composeTestRule.setContent { ArticleRow(Article(id = "42", title = "Hello"), onArticleClick = { clickedId = it }) }
42	    composeTestRule.onNodeWithText("Hello").performClick()
43	    assertEquals("42", clickedId)
44	}
45	```
46	
47	## Choosing the test shape — the smallest contract that proves the behaviour
48	
49	| Proving | Shape |
50	|---|---|
51	| Text rendered, conditional content, loading/error branches, callback wiring | Plain UI Compose test (state + callbacks, no graph) |
52	| Focus navigation, keyboard, TV/D-pad | Compose test with `performKeyInput` + `assertIsFocused()` (see `compose/references/focus-navigation.md`) |
53	| Visual contract semantics can't prove — spacing, themed colour, typography, elevation, gradients, skeletons | Screenshot test, one per meaningful state |
54	| State holder updates UI correctly | State-holder unit test + ONE wiring smoke test |
55	| Lifecycle, navigation, or DI integration itself | Integration test (`createAndroidComposeRule`, Hilt rule, real graph) |
56	
57	**Test clock vs wall clock:** for any Compose-state-observable condition use `mainClock.advanceTimeUntil(ms) { state.value == Done }` (deterministic, fast); use `rule.waitUntil(ms) { … }` only for non-Compose conditions (`Job.isCompleted`, an external counter). Mixing the two in one test is a common flake source.
58	
59	**Animation tests need `mainClock.autoAdvance = false` set *before* `setContent`** — otherwise the framework's `InfiniteAnimationPolicy` throws `CancellationException` on indeterminate animations, and finite animations finish in one auto-advanced burst with no observable intermediate state. After pausing, drive frames with `advanceTimeByFrame()` (kick-off) then `advanceTimeBy(durationMillis)`.
60	
61	**Screenshot determinism:** fixed state data (no current time, random seeds, or remote URLs in the screenshot path); frozen clocks (`Clock.fixed(...)`) and animation progress; a fake image loader for image-heavy screens (Coil 3's test double: `LocalImageLoader provides FakeImageLoader(LocalContext.current)`, or `setContentWithFakeImageLoader { … }`); one shot per meaningful state (loading / error / success / empty), not one per UI element.

2	name: android-debugging
3	description: >
4	  Use when debugging Android or KMP issues — Android-specific techniques covering Logcat, ADB,
5	  ANR traces, R8 stack trace decoding, memory leaks, Gradle build failures, and Compose

8	
9	# Android Debugging
10	
11	## Overview
12	
13	Android-specific evidence-gathering and investigation techniques on a root-cause-first foundation.
14	
15	**Root-cause-first foundation:**
16	- **No fix before the root cause is found.** Investigate first — reproduce, gather evidence (observed values, not assumed), trace the cause. Patching a symptom you don't understand creates two bugs.
17	- **Three failed guesses ⇒ stop and question the architecture** rather than guessing again.
18	
19	The Android-specific tools below serve that investigation. *Optional:* if you run a dedicated debugging-discipline skill (e.g. `superpowers:systematic-debugging` or `ace:systematic-debugging`), this layers on top of it — but it requires none.
20	
21	## Evidence-Gathering by Problem Type
22	
23	### Crashes & Exceptions
24	
25	```bash
26	# Stream crash logs filtered by app package
27	adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s com.example.app)
28	
29	# Save full logcat to file for analysis
30	adb logcat -d > crash_log.txt
31	
32	# Filter by tag
33	adb logcat -s "YourTag:E"
34	```
35	
36	Key logcat log levels: `V` (verbose) `D` (debug) `I` (info) `W` (warn) `E` (error) `F` (fatal)
37	
38	Read the **full stack trace** — the root cause is usually at the bottom of the `Caused by:` chain, not the top-level exception.
39	
40	### ANR (Application Not Responding)
41	
42	ANRs mean the main thread was blocked. Evidence:
43	
44	```bash
45	# Pull ANR trace from device
46	adb pull /data/anr/traces.txt ./anr_traces.txt
47	
48	# Or stream while reproducing
49	adb logcat -s "ActivityManager:E" | grep -A 30 "ANR in"
50	```
51	
52	Look for: `main` thread in state `MONITOR` (waiting for a lock) or blocking I/O on `main`. Trace backward to find what holds the lock.
53	
54	**Common causes:** Database/network call on main thread, `runBlocking` on main thread, deadlock between coroutine scopes.
55	
56	### Memory Leaks
57	
58	Add [LeakCanary](https://square.github.io/leakcanary/) to `debugImplementation`. It surfaces leak traces automatically in a notification.
59	
60	Read the leak trace top-to-bottom: the first bold line is the leaking object, the path shows what's holding the reference. Fix by clearing the reference in the appropriate lifecycle callback.
61	
62	```bash
63	# Dump heap manually for Android Profiler analysis
64	adb shell am dumpheap com.example.app /data/local/tmp/heap.hprof
65	adb pull /data/local/tmp/heap.hprof ./heap.hprof
66	```
67	
68	### Performance Trace Investigation (Perfetto)
69	
70	For bottleneck investigation across CPU, graphics, I/O, IPC, memory, or power — beyond what Logcat and ANR traces show — capture a Perfetto trace and query it with SQL.
71	
72	**Measure before you fix.** For performance regressions, logs usually mislead — capture a *baseline* measurement before changing anything, then bisect against it. A trace tells you where time goes; only a comparison against a known-good baseline tells you what actually regressed.
73	
74	```bash
75	# Capture a trace (system-level, all categories)
76	adb shell perfetto -c - --txt -o /data/misc/perfetto-traces/trace.pftrace \
77	  <<'EOF'
78	buffers { size_kb: 65536 }
79	data_sources { config { name: "linux.ftrace" } }
80	data_sources { config { name: "android.surfaceflinger.frame" } }
81	duration_ms: 10000
82	EOF
83	
84	adb pull /data/misc/perfetto-traces/trace.pftrace ./
85	```
86	
87	Then open the trace at https://ui.perfetto.dev and run SQL against it (`SELECT name, dur FROM slice WHERE dur > 16e6` for frames slower than 16ms, etc.).
88	
89	For an agent-driven workflow — translating an investigation intent (jank, slow startup, battery drain) into the right Perfetto SQL and iterating across the trace — see Google's [`perfetto-sql`](https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/profilers/perfetto-sql) and [`perfetto-trace-analysis`](https://github.com/android/skills/tree/main/profilers/perfetto-trace-analysis) skills (`android skills list` to check for a local install; `android skills add perfetto-sql perfetto-trace-analysis` otherwise). They provide Domain Hints (CPU/Graphics/I/O/IPC/Memory/Power), a mandatory scratchpad chain-of-evidence pattern, and `GLOB`-over-`LIKE` query rules.
90	
91	### R8 / ProGuard — Obfuscated Stack Traces
92	
93	Release crash stack traces are obfuscated. Decode them with the mapping file generated at build time.
94	
95	```bash
96	# retrace a crash (AGP 7+)
97	./gradlew :app:retrace --stacktrace-file crash.txt
98	
99	# Or use the retrace CLI directly
100	java -jar retrace.jar mapping.txt crash.txt
101	```
102	
103	Mapping files are in `app/build/outputs/mapping/<variant>/mapping.txt`. Always archive them alongside release builds.
104	
105	If a class is unexpectedly removed or renamed, add a `-keep` rule in `proguard-rules.pro` and verify with:
106	
107	```bash
108	./gradlew :app:assembleRelease
109	# Then inspect: app/build/outputs/mapping/release/usage.txt (removed) and seeds.txt (kept)
110	```
111	
112	For the **inverse problem** — reading obfuscated third-party code or decoding a stack trace from a library where the mapping file isn't yours — `retrace` doesn't apply. Use `jadx --deobf` (consistent renames across the decompiled output) or `jadx --deobf-map` (when the SDK ships a mapping). The [`android-reverse-engineering` plugin](https://github.com/SimoneAvogadro/android-reverse-engineering-skill) covers the full workflow including the anchor-via-strings strategy for navigating obfuscated code by string literals and framework class names that survive obfuscation (check if it's already installed locally first — it ships as `android-reverse-engineering:*` skills).
113	
114	### Gradle Build Failures
115	
116	Read the error from the **bottom up** — Gradle wraps errors in multiple layers.
117	
118	Common patterns:
119	
120	| Error | Investigation |
121	|-------|--------------|
122	| `Manifest merger failed` | Check `app/build/intermediates/merged_manifests/` for the merged output; look for conflicting `android:` attributes |
123	| `Duplicate class` | Run `./gradlew dependencies` and look for the same class in multiple transitive deps; use `exclude` or force a version |
124	| `Could not resolve` | Check repository declarations, VPN/proxy, dependency version exists |
125	| `D8/R8: Type not present` | Missing `keep` rule or desugaring issue; check `minSdk` vs API used |
126	| `KSP / KAPT error` | Look for the processor's own error above the Gradle wrapper message |
127	
128	```bash
129	# Full dependency tree for a configuration
130	./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath
131	
132	# Run with stacktrace for deeper Gradle errors
133	./gradlew assembleDebug --stacktrace --info 2>&1 | grep -A 20 "FAILED"
134	```
135	
136	### Runtime UI Inspection
137	
138	When a bug is visual (wrong element state, missing content, overlap), dump the layout tree directly instead of reasoning from a screenshot:
139	
140	```bash
141	# Full layout tree as JSON — search by class/text/bounds instead of parsing an image
142	android layout --pretty
143	
144	# Only elements that changed since last call — useful for animations or transient state
145	android layout --diff --pretty
146	
147	# Target a specific device, write to file
148	android layout --device=emulator-5554 -o layout.json
149	```
150	
151	Prefer `android layout` over `adb screencap` whenever the question is "what is the UI state?" rather than "what does it look like?". The JSON tree is grep-able and survives `--diff` state across invocations.
152	
153	### Compose Recomposition Bugs
154	
155	For deeper Compose performance analysis (stability, recomposition skipping, baseline profiles), see `android-skills:compose` → `compose/references/performance.md`.
156	
157	Wrong state or unexpected re-renders:
158	
159	1. **Layout Inspector** (Android Studio) → enable "Show recomposition counts" to identify hot paths. For headless/CLI workflows, `android layout --diff` gives a JSON tree of what changed between frames.
160	2. Add `SideEffect { Log.d("Recompose", "MyComposable recomposed") }` temporarily to confirm
161	3. Check that `State` objects are not created inside the composition (use `remember`)
162	4. Verify `equals()` on state data classes — a new object with same values still triggers recomposition if `equals` is not implemented
163	
164	**Note:** Since Compose compiler 2.0+ (Kotlin 2.0+), strong skipping mode is enabled by default and the compiler automatically memoizes lambdas that capture stable references. Manual `remember {{ }}` wrapping is no longer necessary in most cases. If you see excessive recomposition from lambdas, check whether the captured references are unstable (mutable collections, non-data classes) rather than wrapping in `remember`.
165	
166	(Standard `adb` commands — `devices`, `install -r`, `am start`, `pm clear`, `ps`, `run-as … ls /data/data/<pkg>/` — aren't covered here; for visual-state bugs prefer `android layout` over `screencap` as noted above.)
167	
168	## Multi-Component Evidence Template
169	
170	For issues spanning multiple layers (e.g. Repository → ViewModel → UI):
171	
172	```kotlin
173	// Temporarily instrument each boundary with a UNIQUE run-specific tag
174	// (pick a fresh suffix per session, e.g. DEBUG-a4f2) so the SAME tag both
175	// filters logcat at runtime and greps cleanly at teardown.
176	class UserRepository(...) {
177	    suspend fun fetchUser(id: String): User {
178	        Log.d("DEBUG-a4f2", "Repository: fetching user $id")
179	        val result = api.getUser(id)
180	        Log.d("DEBUG-a4f2", "Repository: received ${result}")
181	        return result
182	    }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	Run once to identify **which layer** produces the bad value. Filter the run at runtime with `adb logcat -s "DEBUG-a4f2"`, then tear the instrumentation back out with a single `grep -rl "DEBUG-a4f2"`. A unique per-session tag is what makes both one-liners work — a shared tag like `DEBUG_LAYER` collides across sessions and leaves orphaned logs behind. Then investigate the implicated layer in isolation before proposing a fix.
187	
188	## Red Flags
189	
190	- Fixing a crash without reading the full `Caused by:` chain
191	- Guessing at an R8 issue without checking the mapping file
192	- Adding `Thread.sleep()` to "fix" an ANR or race condition
193	- Resolving a dependency conflict by adding `exclude` without understanding why the duplicate exists
194	- Fixing a Compose bug by wrapping in `key()` without understanding what triggers recomposition
195	- Leaving temporary instrumentation in the tree — tag every debug log with a unique per-session prefix (e.g. `DEBUG-a4f2`) so cleanup is one `grep`, and remove them all before declaring the fix done

contradictions.claimA: Strict, no exceptions: "No production code without a failing test first. Write the test, watch it fail (RED)... A behaviour you never watched fail isn't proven." A bug isn't fixed until a test that was red because of the bug is green.
contradictions.claimB: Test-first is optional: tests may be written "first (TDD) OR alongside your code" — writing production code before the test is explicitly permitted.
contradictions.evidence: rcosteira: android-testing/SKILL.md lines 17-18. ahmed: ios-testing/SKILL.md line 306 ("Write them first (TDD) or alongside your code, but always maintain them."); note ahmed's mobile-testing/SKILL.md line 97 says "Write tests first" but the iOS skill relaxes it to "or alongside."

bugs.description: The interaction-state example launches the `interactionSource.emit(...)` on a fresh, detached `TestScope()` that is never advanced, so the coroutine body never executes and the interaction is never emitted — the example does not do what it claims. `TestScope()` uses a StandardTestDispatcher whose scheduler only runs tasks when explicitly pumped (runCurrent/advanceUntilIdle); the following `composeTestRule.waitForIdle()` synchronizes Compose's own work, not this unrelated TestScope. The subsequent 'assert the visual/semantic change that hover produces' therefore asserts against the un-hovered state. Ironically the skill correctly warns not to use `LaunchedEffect` but substitutes an equally non-working driver.
bugs.evidence: Lines 97-105: `TestScope().launch { interactionSource.emit(HoverInteraction.Enter()) }` followed by `composeTestRule.waitForIdle()` with no scheduler advancement. Correct approaches would emit from the test's own coroutine (e.g. within `runTest`/`runComposeUiTest` and advance) or via `composeTestRule` clock, not a detached TestScope.

bugs.description: The ViewModel test constructs `HomeViewModel(repository)` and drives it with `runTest {}` but installs no MainDispatcherRule / `Dispatchers.setMain(...)`. A standard Android ViewModel launches work in `viewModelScope`, which is bound to `Dispatchers.Main`; without replacing Main in a JVM unit test the test throws `IllegalStateException: Module with the Main dispatcher had failed to initialize`. This is exactly the setup rcosteira's android-testing skill warns about (the two-schedulers trap), and it is absent here.
bugs.evidence: Lines 29-49: `@BeforeEach setup(){ ...; viewModel = HomeViewModel(repository) }` and `fun \`loads items successfully\`() = runTest { ... viewModel.onIntent(LoadItems) ... }` with no MainDispatcherRule anywhere in the skill. Contrast rcosteira android-testing/SKILL.md line 26 (pass `mainRule.dispatcher` into `runTest`).

bugs.description: The Turbine StateFlow test asserts the loading state as the FIRST emission, but `stateFlow.test {}` replays the current (initial) value first. `onIntent(LoadItems)` is called before the first `awaitItem()`, and the initial state (isLoading almost certainly false) is what the first `awaitItem()` returns, so `awaitItem().isLoading shouldBe true` asserts against the wrong item. Correct pattern is to consume/skip the initial item first, then trigger the action; with StandardTestDispatcher the loading emission may also be conflated away without an explicit advance.
bugs.evidence: Lines 43-47: `viewModel.state.test { viewModel.onIntent(LoadItems); awaitItem().isLoading shouldBe true; awaitItem().items shouldBe listOf(item) }` — no initial `awaitItem()`/`skipItems(1)` before triggering the intent.

bugs.description: The Espresso flaky-fix snippet uses `@IdlingResource` as an annotation on a property, but there is no such annotation — `androidx.test.espresso.IdlingResource` is an interface. The snippet will not compile and teaches a nonexistent API; a `CountingIdlingResource` is used by registering it via `IdlingRegistry.getInstance().register(...)`, not by annotating a field. `@get:Rule val disableAnimationsRule = DisableAnimationsRule()` also references a non-standard/undefined class.
bugs.evidence: Lines 116-124: `@IdlingResource val countingIdlingResource = CountingIdlingResource("api")` and `@get:Rule val disableAnimationsRule = DisableAnimationsRule()`.

bugs.description: Presents wrapping content in `CompositionLocalProvider(LocalInspectionMode provides true)` as the fix strategy for Compose test flakiness whose listed causes are 'Recomposition timing / State hoisting issues / Animation interference.' `LocalInspectionMode` is a preview/inspection flag; it does not control recomposition timing, state hoisting, or the test clock, so it is not a remedy for those flake causes. The correct levers (per rcosteira) are `mainClock.autoAdvance=false` before setContent, `advanceTimeByFrame()`, and `mainClock.advanceTimeUntil { ... }`.
bugs.evidence: Lines 135-150: under 'Compose Tests ... Common Flaky Causes: Recomposition timing / State hoisting issues / Animation interference', the 'Fix Strategies' block is `CompositionLocalProvider(LocalInspectionMode provides true){ content() }`.
